A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CapsIE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v3 reports original CapsIE classification, rotation prediction, colour prediction, retrieval and capsule-count experiments on 3DIEBench, including Tables 1–3 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds Objaverse-LVIS transfer results and MOVi-E detection, classification and pose results in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The core CapsIE architecture is retained. v4 adds a downstream DETR adaptation with a quaternion-regression MLP and additional MSE loss for MOVi-E (Section 4.5.2). Corrections to the original loss description do not establish that the previously implemented CapsIE training procedure changed.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates 3DIEBench. v4 adds randomly rotated, multi-view Objaverse-LVIS objects from six classes and MOVi-E frames containing multiple objects, occlusions and complex backgrounds. Coverage expands to cross-dataset transfer, object detection and per-object camera-relative pose estimation.

E2.justification: SEN is newly evaluated in the Objaverse-LVIS comparison in v4 Table 4. The existing 3DIEBench comparator sets remain unchanged. VICReg, SimCLR, AugSelf, EquiMod and SIE were already represented in v3's comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 introduces frozen-backbone versus full-network fine-tuning protocols on Objaverse-LVIS. MOVi-E adds frozen ResNet-50 features, DETR training for 200 epochs with batch size 64 and a scheduled learning rate, and detection mAP metrics. Existing 3DIEBench training and downstream evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: The capsule-count analysis remains unchanged. v4 adds substantive transfer analyses: frozen versus fine-tuned use of 3DIEBench representations on Objaverse-LVIS, and transfer from isolated-object training to crowded, occluded MOVi-E scenes. These test representation adaptability and generalization under distribution shifts.

E5.justification: v4 Section 4.1 newly states that most experiments use one run with seed 2224. Table 4 reports means and standard deviations across five evaluation seeds. v3 provides no corresponding seed or run-count disclosure; repeated-run uncertainty reporting remains limited to the new Objaverse experiment.

E6.justification: Matching 3DIEBench results are unchanged. New Table 4 reports frozen-backbone rotation R2 of 0.43±0.014 for CapsIE versus 0.29±0.005 for SIE, alongside lower classification accuracy. New Table 5 reports MOVi-E mAP of 28.26 versus 26.47 and rotation R2 of 0.23 versus 0.20, but classification of 72.5 versus 73.7. These are additional results under new settings.

T1.justification: The final objective changes the mean-entropy terms from addition in v3 Equation 6 to subtraction in v4 Equation 5, correcting the inconsistency with entropy maximization. The existing group definitions and equivariance equation are moved to Appendix A.2 without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the principal architecture, objective, efficiency and 3DIEBench performance claims. The conclusion replaces the claim that additional transformations are preserved without prior knowledge with a narrower claim of learning objective-specified equivariance.

C2.justification: v4 attributes weak colour prediction to rotation-focused training, explains online versus downstream evaluation differences, and interprets the new transfer results. It adds capacity and single-run limitations while removing v3's specific warning about scaling capsule depth. The new discussion incorrectly associates negative R2 with negative correlation.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies Tait-Bryan angles versus quaternion encoding, identifies the 22-hour runtime with the 32-capsule model, and adds SIE's 26-hour runtime. It supplies MOVi-E head dimensions, loss weights and training details. The existing code pointer and original appendix protocol tables are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Section 5.3 on part–whole decomposition and interpretability, cites stacked capsule autoencoders and works supporting the new benchmarks and DETR adaptation, and removes the Mitterreiter and Nair scaling references. Several other bibliography changes merely update previously cited works to published versions.

P1.justification: v4 copyedits prose throughout, shortens Section 2 by moving formal definitions to Appendix A.2, consolidates the appendices under A, and rewrites the concluding discussion. The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: A new document template changes the title and author layout, typography, headings, captions and spacing throughout. Tables 4–5 are added, and the original appendix benchmark tables, now Tables 9–10, share the final page. All five existing figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation beyond v3's single-dataset study through transfer to Objaverse-LVIS and complex MOVi-E scenes, with five-seed uncertainty reporting for Objaverse. It also corrects the entropy-loss sign and better aligns the conclusion with the weak colour-prediction results. Most experiments remain single-run, and the new negative-R2 interpretation is erroneous, but these limitations do not outweigh the broader generalization evidence and clearer mathematical specification.
